entries.notes: Named-pipe wire contract (serializer/field ids) for the 'dotnet test' <-> Microsoft.Testing.Platform protocol. MUST stay byte-aligned with testfx: ids are the on-wire identity and cannot change without a coordinated protocol break. testfx is the source of truth (its copy is packed by DotnetTestProtocolContract.props). CoverageSummary (file-artifact field 9) and CoverageSummaryMessages (serializer 15) are already implemented in the SDK. RetryAttemptNumber and IsSuperseded are reserved in the SDK contract so newer peers can send them without conflicting ids; the SDK does not consume that metadata until its serializers and retry model support framework-level retry attempts. ProviderUid, MinimumArity, and MaximumArity are also reserved; the SDK's command-line option serializer skips that optional metadata.

sources.scope: entire file; ids must match exactly

entries.notes: Handshake/session/state string constants for the 'dotnet test' named-pipe protocol. Upstream lives in testfx IPC/Constants.cs; the SDK inlines the same constants into CliConstants.cs (TestStates, SessionEventTypes, HandshakeMessagePropertyNames, HandshakeMessageExecutionModes, HandshakeMessageHostTypes, ProtocolConstants). Watch the upstream file for added/changed wire constants. The SDK mirrors the ArtifactPostProcessor and TestHostOrchestrator host types, the OrchestratorFeature property, and the 'tool' execution mode. GitHub Actions workflow commands use informational DisplayMessage (1.3.0+) so the SDK writes their text verbatim without warning/error formatting. CoverageSummaryVersion (handshake field 20, version '1') is already implemented and negotiated independently of the base protocol. The SDK consumes the retry orchestrator feature to enable retry UX before the first TestHost handshake. Intentional divergences: the SDK does not mirror TestStates.InProgress, and ProtocolConstants.SupportedVersions deliberately stops at 1.3.0 because the SDK does not implement the 1.4.0 reverse server-control channel.

The Microsoft.Testing.Platform terminal UI reporter, hard-forked into 'dotnet test'. This entry tracks the reporter class, including its SDK partial files. Each upstream partial is tracked so any upstream reporter change pings the SDK to reconcile. Upstream includes the whole folder via a glob (TerminalReporterContract.props), so new partials must be appended here -- see microsoft/testfx#10390. Sources are append-only: the tracking issue marker keys on the source index. CI progress and summary ordering are reconciled through f4d8d35b: visible-silence heartbeats include finished modules, compact non-cursor summaries put verdicts and failure recaps before artifacts, and successful module summaries are not repeated when already printed at completion. Existing retry/flaky, slowest-test, visibility, and neutral zero-test behavior is retained. The SDK's final aggregate exit code remains authoritative for session/handshake/policy failures and ignored exit codes, rather than upstream's in-process HasTestSessionFailure callback. SDK-specific collection progress/status and incomplete live-result warnings do not infer test outcomes from discovery, maps, or recovered artifacts. Coverage measurements use the independently negotiated CoverageSummaryVersion=1 IPC contract; the SDK's TerminalTestReporter.Coverage.cs renders application-scoped measurements and complete merged-artifact totals without summing applications. Coverage threshold rendering remains unported because threshold messages have no representation in this IPC contract; evaluation and exit codes remain application-owned. Other intentional divergences: framework-level retry attribution needs IPC metadata, so retries remain attributed per test-host instance; ShowRunSummary remains enabled because the SDK owns one whole-run aggregate; in-process structured progress messages have no SDK IPC representation. This is a hard fork: the signal is upstream changed, not files differ.

Terminal reporter options hard-forked from testfx. Heartbeat and slow-test thresholds default to 60 seconds; the SDK retains its synchronous boolean ShowProgress and adds collection-mode classification. Captured stdout and stderr default to Failed in every environment, with independent per-module all/failed/none overrides. Raw process output, capture, and test-result visibility remain independent. Existing retry/flaky, slowest-test, and zero-test options are retained. The SDK uses the final aggregate exit code instead of the upstream in-process HasTestSessionFailure and ZeroTestsPolicy callbacks.

Terminal reporter support type hard-forked from testfx. The upstream Results/Summary partial split changes file organization, so the SDK keeps its single-file fork and tracks both new partials below. The SDK implements instance-based retry/flaky accounting; framework-level retry attribution still needs IPC metadata. HasIncompleteTestResults is SDK-owned session-lifecycle state, not a recovered-artifact count. RuntimeFramework is immutable execution metadata separate from TargetFramework and Architecture; the SDK appends its constructor argument after existing retry/visibility settings.

entries.notes: Visible-output silence, cumulative results, completion age, and exponential slow-test reporting. SDK adapts namespace/resources and retains GetRunningTasks(1).FirstOrDefault() semantics rather than importing unrelated allocation optimizations. Slow-test descriptions use the shared target/process/runtime display helper.
Exponential slow-test backoff, with only the namespace and repository header adapted.
GetProgressThreshold adapts upstream nonnegative-integer parsing to SDK environment access. Both heartbeat and slow-test defaults are 60 seconds; zero disables that signal.

TerminalProgressHeartbeat*, TerminalProgressSlowTest, ErroredAssembliesHeader and RuntimeFramework are adapted into the managed CLI resource owner. Captured-output help descriptions are adapted into CommandDefinitionStrings.resx so the SDK advertises its Failed default even when an older test application supplies help metadata. SDK-only collection and reporting-completeness messages have no upstream equivalent. Upstream ANSI/progress option descriptions are not vendored; their removal/renaming at 74be6a61 needs no resource port. The SDK retains its own --no-ansi and --no-progress options and descriptions.
